issues.concern: The top-level gloss 'school year, grade level' is a bit redundant with the more detailed definitions below. It could be more concise or representative of both senses without being a direct list of them.
issues.suggestion: Consider a more encompassing or slightly different phrasing for the top-level gloss, such as 'academic year; grade level' or 'school year; grade'.

issues.concern: The English translation 'Studying gets harder as you advance in grade level' is a bit clunky. 'Studying' as a general subject is less natural than 'the studies' or 'the work'.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'The studies get harder as you advance in grade level.' or 'The work gets harder as you advance in grade level.'

issues.concern: The English translation 'Year-end exams are approaching' is slightly less natural than 'The year-end exams are approaching' or 'Year-end exams are drawing near'.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'The year-end exams are approaching.' or 'Year-end exams are drawing near.'

issues.concern: The English translation 'classes were reshuffled' is a bit informal and less common in an educational context than 'classes were rearranged' or 'class assignments were changed'.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'The new school year started and classes were rearranged.' or 'The new school year started and class assignments were changed.'
